lessons.title: A reason, a thank-you and an accusation
lessons.description: Follow a disrupted route and distinguish appreciative or negative attribution.
lessons.canDo: Identify a reason and the speaker’s stance

lessons.title: A report keeps what is still unknown
lessons.description: Read the update time, the event sequence and the limit of a cause claim.
lessons.canDo: Separate a reported reason from an unproved cause

grammar.title: Credit a benefit; notice sarcasm
grammar.formation: Attributive plain verb/い-adjective + おかげで; noun のおかげで; な-adjective なおかげで. Past/negative clauses keep their conjugation.
grammar.explanation: Usually credits a helpful cause with appreciation. Misaki thanks a friend for showing an alternative route. Negative sarcastic use also exists: wording, context and delivery matter. A thankful sentence states the speaker’s attribution; it doesn’t prove that no other factors helped.
grammar.example: 道順を教えてくれたおかげで、無事に着きました。
grammar.translation: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely.

examples.ja: {道順|みちじゅん}を{教|おし}えてくれたおかげで、{無事|ぶじ}に{着|つ}きました。
examples.en: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely.

examples.ja: {点検|てんけん}が{丁寧|ていねい}なおかげで、{不具合|ふぐあい}に{気|き}づきました。
examples.en: Thanks to the careful inspection, we noticed the problem.

examples.ja: 「{君|きみ}のおかげで{遅刻|ちこく}したよ」は、ここでは{皮肉|ひにく}です。
examples.en: “Thanks to you I was late” is sarcastic here.

grammar.mistake: Noun + の, na-adjective + な. Do not label every おかげで result positive, or infer sole causation from a thank-you. Sarcasm is labelled recognition here, not the default way to thank someone.

grammar.title: Hear a negative attribution without certifying blame
grammar.formation: Attributive plain verb/い-adjective + せいで; noun のせいで; な-adjective なせいで. Sentence-final せいだ/せいです.
grammar.explanation: Normally attributes an unwanted result to a cause, sometimes blaming someone. The scene identifies transport disruption, then refuses to assume that a particular worker caused the electrical problem. A speaker’s せいで claim may be justified or mistaken; the grammar alone cannot settle responsibility.
grammar.example: 乗り場が混雑したせいで、発車が遅れました。
grammar.translation: Because the boarding point became crowded, departure was delayed.

examples.ja: {乗|の}り{場|ば}が{混雑|こんざつ}したせいで、{発車|はっしゃ}が{遅|おく}れました。
examples.en: Because the boarding point became crowded, departure was delayed.

examples.ja: {強風|きょうふう}のせいで、{看板|かんばん}が{倒|たお}れました。
examples.en: The sign fell because of the strong wind.

examples.ja: {説明|せつめい}が{不十分|ふじゅうぶん}なせいで、{戸惑|とまど}いました。
examples.en: I was confused because the explanation was insufficient.

grammar.mistake: Use nominal のせいで rather than だせいで. Undesirable attribution is the usual use, not a universal ban on all other nuances. Do not treat a quoted blame claim as a checked cause.

grammar.title: Read ため as cause or purpose in context
grammar.formation: Attributive verb/い-adjective clause + ため(に); noun のため(に); な-adjective なため(に). Past and negative clauses are allowed; に is often omitted in notices.
grammar.explanation: Purpose ために was taught in unit 1. Here an outage is given as the reason for cancelled morning service. Causal ため often occurs in reports with completed events, but present states and negative causes also work. Identify the relation between the clauses rather than deciding by tense alone. Neutral wording doesn’t independently certify the reported cause.
grammar.example: 停電のため、朝の電車は運休でした。
grammar.translation: Morning trains were cancelled due to the power outage.

examples.ja: {停電|ていでん}のため、{朝|あさ}の{電車|でんしゃ}は{運休|うんきゅう}でした。
examples.en: Morning trains were cancelled due to the power outage.

examples.ja: {設備|せつび}が{使|つか}えないため、{開始|かいし}{時刻|じこく}を{変|か}えます。
examples.en: Because the equipment cannot be used, we’ll change the start time.

examples.ja: {混雑|こんざつ}を{防止|ぼうし}するために、{入口|いりぐち}を{分|わ}けます。
examples.en: We separate the entrances to prevent crowding.

grammar.mistake: Noun + のため, na-adjective + なため. The third example is deliberate purpose; the first two are cause. Past tense is a clue, not a complete purpose/cause rule.

grammar.title: Give a reason for a request
grammar.formation: Plain/polite clause + から; plain present noun/な-adjective + だから. Attributive clause + ので; present noun/な-adjective + なので; polite ですので. Past/negative clauses conjugate before the connector.
grammar.explanation: Retrieve から and ので. Both can give reasons for an action or a suitable request. ので often presents a softer explanation, while から can foreground the speaker’s reason; these are tendencies. Neither proves that the explanation is objectively true. The task names the form when testing attachment and states the listener when requesting help.
grammar.example: 運休なので、別の経路を教えてください。
grammar.translation: Since the service is cancelled, please tell me another route.

examples.ja: {運休|うんきゅう}なので、{別|べつ}の{経路|けいろ}を{教|おし}えてください。
examples.en: Since the service is cancelled, please tell me another route.

examples.ja: {点検|てんけん}が{終|お}わりましたので、{運行|うんこう}を{再開|さいかい}します。
examples.en: The inspection has finished, so we’ll resume service.

examples.ja: {渋滞|じゅうたい}が{心配|しんぱい}だから、{早|はや}く{出|で}よう。
examples.en: I’m worried about traffic congestion, so let’s leave early.

grammar.mistake: Nominal 運休なので needs な; 運休だから has だ. ので is not restricted to statements without requests, and から is not automatically rude. Do not force a unique synonym choice when both fit.

dialogues.title: A disrupted route and a thank-you
dialogues.scene: Monday morning, after Saturday’s film gathering, a line is out of service following a Sunday-night outage. Misaki takes a bus and walks. This is an original fictional scenario, not real transport advice.

lines.line: {月曜日|げつようび}の{朝|あさ}、{停電|ていでん}のために{電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}していると{知|し}りました。
lines.romaji: Getsuyōbi no asa, teiden no tame ni densha ga unkyū shite iru to shirimashita.
lines.meaning: On Monday morning I learned that trains were out of service because of a power outage.

lines.speaker: Kenta

lines.romaji: Nichiyōbi no yoru ni okita teiden da ne. Doyōbi no eiga wa yotei dōri owatta yo.
lines.meaning: That’s the outage that occurred Sunday night. Saturday’s film ended as scheduled.

lines.speaker: Misaki

lines.romaji: Noriba no konzatsu to jūtai no sei de, basu no hassha mo okuremashita.
lines.meaning: The bus departure was delayed too because of crowding at the boarding point and traffic congestion.

lines.meaning: I’ll send the route for after you get off the bus. Use the sign at the corner as a landmark.

lines.romaji: Michijun o oshiete kureta okage de, buji ni mokutekichi ni tsukimashita. Arigatō.
lines.meaning: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely at the destination. Thank you.

lines.meaning: The trains are still stopped, then. Are you taking the bus home too?

lines.romaji: Kaeru mae ni, unkō no jōhō o kakunin shimashō.
lines.meaning: Let’s check the service update before you head home.

lines.meaning: The morning information session has been moved to four in the afternoon, right?

lines.romaji: Ja, yoji made sukoshi yasumō. Basu, kondete tsukareta desho.
lines.meaning: Let’s rest a bit until four. That crowded bus must’ve been tiring.

dialogues.title: An update with a limited claim
dialogues.scene: Monday at three in the afternoon, Bao and Yamamoto prepare a short fictional update. Service restoration is reported, the electrical cause remains under investigation, and the information session has not yet started.

lines.romaji: Gogo sanji desu. Unkō ga fukkyū shita to iu happyō o kakunin shimashita.
lines.meaning: It’s three in the afternoon. I have checked the announcement that service has been restored.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Tenken ga owatta node, unkō o saikai shita to iu setsumei desu ne.
lines.meaning: The explanation is that service resumed because the inspection was completed, right?

lines.romaji: Hai. Setsubi ni fuguai ga hassei shita sō desu ga, sono yōin wa mada chōsa chū desu.
lines.meaning: Yes. A problem reportedly occurred with the equipment, but its contributing factors are still under investigation.

lines.speaker: You

lines.romaji: Sō nan desu ne. Saikai shita jikan mo, kiji ni ireta hō ga ii desu ka?
lines.meaning: I see. Should I include the time service resumed in the article too?

lines.romaji: Hai. Unkō no saikai to, setsumeikai no kaishi jikoku o kaite kudasai.
lines.meaning: Yes. Include the service resumption and the start time of the information session.

lines.romaji: Buntan dōri, watashi ga yōyaku o hikiukemasu. Betsu no keiro no annai mo iremasu.
lines.meaning: As assigned, I’ll take on the summary. I’ll include guidance on the alternative route too.

lines.meaning: The information session starts at four. Even though service has been restored, we’ll not change that decision.

lines.romaji: Kakunin ni wa tema ga kakarimasu ga, teinei ni kaite kureta okage de, naiyō ga wakariyasui desu.
lines.meaning: Checking takes effort, but thanks to your careful writing, the content is easy to understand.

lines.meaning: Thank you. I’ll post this update before the four-o’clock start.

readings.title: Service restored; the session still starts at four

{午前|ごぜん}の{説明会|せつめいかい}は、{午後|ごご}{四時|よじ}に{変|か}わった。この{決定|けってい}は{復旧|ふっきゅう}{後|ご}も{変|か}えない。{参加者|さんかしゃ}には{連絡|れんらく}{済|ず}みで、{開始|かいし}{前|まえ}に{再|ふたた}び{案内|あんない}する。{土曜日|どようび}の{映画|えいが}は{予定|よてい}どおり{終|お}わっており、{今回|こんかい}の{運休|うんきゅう}とは{別|べつ}の{出来事|できごと}だ。{分|わ}かっていることと{分|わ}からないことを{省略|しょうりゃく}せずに、{情報|じょうほう}を{要約|ようやく}した。

options: Sunday night, after the Saturday film had ended

exercises.explain: Kenta separates Sunday night from the completed Saturday film.

exercises.prompt: What does Misaki specifically thank Bao for?
options: Explaining the route after getting off the bus
Causing the power outage
Cancelling viewer subtitle choice
exercises.explain: Her 道順を教えてくれたおかげで credits the route guidance.

exercises.prompt: What reasons does Misaki give for the delayed bus departure?
options: Crowding at the boarding point and traffic congestion
Heavy snow and a closed airport
A confirmed fault by a named employee
exercises.explain: She states 乗り場の混雑と渋滞のせいで; no named employee is blamed.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the stated na-adjective pattern 丁寧なおかげで, with 丁寧 before the blank.

options: な
の
だ
exercises.explain: 丁寧 is a na-adjective, so its attributive attachment here is な.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named noun pattern 強風のせいで.
exercises.line: {強風|きょうふう}＿＿せいで、{看板|かんばん}が{倒|たお}れました。
options: の
な
だ
exercises.explain: 強風 is a noun; の connects it to せいで.

exercises.context: You are speaking politely to the friend who offered an alternative route. Thank them and request it.
exercises.line: {別|べつ}の{経路|けいろ}を{送|おく}ります。
options: ありがとうございます。{電車|でんしゃ}が{運休|うんきゅう}なので、{教|おし}えてください。
{君|きみ}のせいだ。{道順|みちじゅん}は{聞|き}かない。
{土曜日|どようび}の{映画|えいが}はまだ{始|はじ}まっていませんね。
exercises.explain: The first accepts the offered help politely; the others accuse or contradict the stated Saturday chronology.

exercises.meaning: Thanks to your explaining the route, I arrived safely at the destination.

exercises.explain: Route guidance is the credited help, followed by the completed safe arrival.

exercises.prompt: What has Yamamoto checked at three in the afternoon?
options: An announcement that service has been restored
That a particular person caused the outage
That the session is already over
exercises.explain: The first line checks the restoration announcement, not private fault or the completed session.

exercises.prompt: Which point is still under investigation?
options: The factors behind the equipment problem
Whether Saturday’s film ended
Whether Bao has been assigned the summary
exercises.explain: Yamamoto explicitly says 要因はまだ調査中.

options: The information session starts at four
All trains remain cancelled forever
The Saturday film will start on Monday
exercises.explain: 運行が復旧しても leaves the four-o’clock decision unchanged.

exercises.prompt: What work does Bao agree to take on?
options: Write the summary and include the alternative route
Cancel the four-o’clock session
Send only a photograph of the equipment
exercises.explain: Bao accepts the summary task and says he will include guidance on the alternative route.

exercises.context: Form practice: complete the named noun-cause pattern 停電のため.
exercises.line: {停電|ていでん}＿＿ため、{朝|あさ}の{電車|でんしゃ}は{運休|うんきゅう}でした。
options: の
な
だ
exercises.explain: 停電 is a noun followed by のため; the reported outcome is cancellation, not a goal to create an outage.

exercises.context: Form practice: use the named nominal reason 運休なので, not a synonym choice between から and ので.
exercises.line: {運休|うんきゅう}＿＿ので、{別|べつ}の{経路|けいろ}を{教|おし}えてください。
options: な
の
だ
exercises.explain: The noun 運休 uses なので in this pattern; the suitable request is permitted.

exercises.context: Reply politely to Yamamoto-san: confirm that your summary will retain what is still unknown.
exercises.line: {分|わ}からないことも{省略|しょうりゃく}しないでください。
options: はい。{不明|ふめい}な{点|てん}も{要約|ようやく}に{入|い}れます。
まだ{調査|ちょうさ}{中|ちゅう}ですが、{原因|げんいん}は{絶対|ぜったい}に{雷|かみなり}です。
うん、{先生|せんせい}の{本音|ほんね}は{全部|ぜんぶ}{分|わ}かるよ。
exercises.explain: The first confirms the organizer’s request politely. The second asserts an unproved cause; the third guesses private thoughts and fails the requested style.

exercises.meaning: Morning trains were cancelled due to the power outage.
exercises.explain: The outage is the reported cause; the cancelled morning service is the completed consequence.

exercises.context: Use the stated update, not assumptions about unstated causes or later events.
exercises.prompt: At the time of this update, what is true about the session?
options: It’s still scheduled for four; the update is at three
It finished at three before the update
It has returned to the original morning time
exercises.explain: Three is the update time; four remains the start after service restoration.

exercises.context: Use the stated update, not assumptions about unstated causes or later events.
exercises.prompt: What conclusion does the report refuse to establish from the thunder alone?
options: That it caused the equipment problem
That thunder occurred on the same night
That train service was cancelled in the morning
exercises.explain: Same-night thunder is reported, but 因果関係 remains unsupported; the other two statements are explicit.

exercises.context: Use the stated update, not assumptions about unstated causes or later events.
exercises.prompt: Which action is still planned before the four-o’clock start?
options: Giving participants another notice
Restoring the already completed Saturday film
Announcing a verified culprit
exercises.explain: The report says 開始前に再び案内する; prior contact is already complete.

watch.prompt: Optionally save a cause or thank-you line from your own clip. Record the stated reason, the speaker’s stance and which causes remain unconfirmed. This is observation, not a scored causal experiment.
